sumInsured: Not specified in extracted text (varies as per Policy Schedule; illustrations show ₹3,00,000)

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with the Company.
good.reference: Section 4.1(a)(ii) Specific Waiting Period – Code- Excl02
good.explanation: Listed diseases/surgeries are not covered until you complete 24 months of continuous coverage. Claims for these conditions will be payable only from the 3rd policy year onward.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are excluded for the first 36 months of continuous coverage. You need to stay insured for 3 years before PED-related claims become payable.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Section 4.1(a)(iii) First 30-Day waiting Period – Code – Excl03
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered in the first 30 days, while accidents are covered immediately. This is a standard waiting period that can affect claims soon after buying the policy.

good.name: Room Rent
good.quote: If the Insured Person is admitted in a room where the Room Category is other than Single Private Room with A.C., then the Policyholder shall bear the ratable proportion of the total Associate Medical Expenses... in the proportion of the difference between the Room Rent of Single Private Room with A.C. to the Room Rent actually incurred.
good.reference: Section 3.1(c)(i) Conditions for Medical Expenses – Room Category
good.explanation: Coverage is aligned to a Single Private Room with A.C. and choosing any other room category triggers a ratable (proportionate) share of associated medical expenses. Upgrading rooms can significantly increase your out-of-pocket costs beyond just the room rent difference.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: As Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses' during a period of 30 days immediately prior to the date of the Insured Person's admission to the Hospital;
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for up to 30 days before hospitalization if related to the same condition. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: As Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses' during a period of 60 days immediately following the date of the Insured Person's discharge from Hospital,
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for up to 60 days after discharge if related to the same condition. This supports follow-up visits, diagnostics, and medicines during recovery.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.quote: Not found in the provided policy wording extract.
bad.explanation: No restore/reinstatement benefit is evidenced in the provided extract. Once the Sum Insured is exhausted, you may not get any automatic refill for further hospitalizations in the same policy year.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – II to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.explanation: Items listed as non-medical consumables in Annexure II are excluded from payment. This can lead to frequent out-of-pocket costs for common hospital items like gloves, masks, syringes, etc.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: For diseases or conditions or procedure that have a specified sub-limit then all related expenses shall be covered up to the sub-limit specified for that disease or condition or procedure.
bad.explanation: Some diseases/procedures can have their own sub-limits, and all related expenses are payable only up to that cap. Even with a high Sum Insured, your payout can be restricted for those listed conditions.

bad.name: Modern Treatments
bad.quote: Expenses related to any kind of Advance Technology Methods other than mentioned in the Clause 3.1(d).
bad.explanation: Advanced technology methods are excluded unless they are specifically listed under Clause 3.1(d). This can limit coverage for newer procedures if they are not explicitly named in the covered list.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: The Policyholder shall bear 20% of the Final Claim Amount... *Entry Age means the age of the Insured Person at the time of issue of the first Policy... (b) The Co-payment shall be applicable to each and every Claim, for each Insured Person.
bad.explanation: A 20% co-pay applies to each and every claim for an insured person whose entry age is 60 years or above. This means you will always pay 20% of the approved claim amount out of pocket, which is a major cost burden in senior years.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: Network Provider... For an updated list of Network Provider... can refer to the list of Network Provider available on the Company's website or at the call centre.
unclear.explanation: The policy directs you to the insurer’s website/call centre for the current list of network providers. Since the number of hospitals is not stated here, you should verify network availability in your city before buying.
